newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends higher on BOK dollar sales.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends higher on BOK dollar sales.

text.p: The won closed higher against the dollar on Friday due to the central bank's dollar sales and exporter settlements, dealers said.
The won closed at 864.90 after opening at an intraday low of 866.00, which was also the lowest level since the market average system was introduced in March 1990.
"Trading was quiet after yesterday's rally," said a domestic bank dealer.
Dealers said the dollar's rise against the yen on world markets and rising trade deficit limited the won's rise.
The won's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 865.10 on Monday, compared with 864.50 on Friday, dealers said.
They said the Bank of Korea sold dollars in early trading at 864.00/865.00 won per dollar to stop the won's fall.
The bank denied intervening, as it routinely does.
Dealers forecast trading would range from 864.00 to 868.00 next week.
"The dollar-yen rate and the central bank's intervention will be main market-moving factors next week," said a foreign bank dealer.
